mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.0% consistently signals accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 4.0% indicates labor market deterioration that precedes corporate earnings declines, generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.0% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales signal broad consumer demand weakness that triggers S&P 500 sell-offs over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing industrial production growth during late-cycle expansions typically reduces manufacturing output and corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO growth is negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: CPI inflation exceeding 2.5% monthly signals persistent inflation that triggers Fed tightening expectations, depressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL monthly change exceeds 2.5% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent unemployment rate increases and non-farm payrolls declines indicate severe labor market contraction that precedes earnings deterioration and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of rising UNRATE and falling PAYEMS fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During post-recession recoveries, accelerating retail sales growth consistently drives corporate revenue expansion and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods during post-recession recovery when RSAFS growth is positive over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained retail sales growth consistently correlates with rising consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in less than 55% of periods when RSAFS growth is positive over a 3-year rolling window.
